what_it_does: Sparse triangular solve (SpTRSV) is a mathematical operation used in scientific simulation and engineering software: given a triangular system of equations where most coefficients are zero (sparse), find the unknown values. It is notoriously hard to parallelize because each answer depends on the answers computed before it (a chain of data dependencies). Existing FPGA (reprogrammable chip) accelerators exploit parallelism only within a small block of the matrix (intra-tile), missing opportunities to run multiple blocks simultaneously (inter-tile). HiSpTRSV analyzes the dependency graph between tiles — a map of which blocks must finish before others can start — to identify tiles that are safe to compute at the same time. It then manages the communication between concurrent tiles and balances the uneven workloads that arise from irregular sparse patterns, achieving faster end-to-end solve times on FPGAs.
